Common paths are: major in hotel management/tourism or join directly → start as a receptionist → become familiar with the reservation and room status system → be promoted to shift manager/guest relations specialist, or move to sales, operations and other positions.

Suitable for people who have a stable temperament, love to deal with people, and can handle multiple things at the same time. If you can answer the phone and check in at the same time, and still smile sincerely to each guest, this career is suitable for you.

Hotel front desk clerks (Hotel, Motel, And Resort Desk Clerks) are responsible for guests' check-in, check-out, reservations, inquiries and accounting processing, coordinating guest rooms, catering and other departments to meet guest needs. They are the front desk window position for hotel reception services.

entries: Hotel front desk clerks are responsible for guests' check-in, check-out, reservations, inquiries and accounting processing, and coordinate various departments such as guest rooms and catering to meet guest needs. They are the front desk window positions for hotel reception services.
Handle guests' check-in and check-out procedures, verify identity, assign room cards and process deposits.
Handle phone and online reservations, check room status, confirm orders and make changes and cancellations.
Answer guest inquiries and provide information services such as transportation, catering, and surrounding tours.
Coordinate with guest room, concierge, catering and other departments to handle special needs and complaints from guests.
Reconcile accounts and bills, handle charges, invoices and shift handover reconciliations.
Maintain the front desk environment and guest information, record shift handover information and emergencies.

paragraphs: A computer and a phone are the battlefield: when checking in, you must make sure your ID, room card, and deposit are correct; the phone is ringing, guests are queuing up, and the manager is behind to urge you to report. You have to get everything in place within a few minutes. The night shift is relatively quiet, but you have to deal with emergencies alone.

In one sentence: check in, check out, take reservations, answer questions, settle accounts. Specifically, it includes check-in and check-out procedures, reservation and room status management, inquiry services, department coordination, account verification and shift handover records.

But medium and high exposure does not mean high risk: the more automated the process, the more people are needed to deal with customers that cannot be accommodated by automation. Those who are squeezed are the front desk staff who can only click the mouse to complete the process. People who can serve and adapt are more in demand.

Study hotel management and tourism management, and do many internships at school. In the AI ​​​​era, employees should no longer only handle formalities, but focus on practicing foreign languages, complaint handling and operational thinking, and move towards duty managers and guest relations.

Familiarize yourself with self-service devices and AI tools, and focus on experience services. Take the hotel management-related certificate and be promoted to duty manager, front office operation or sales. Don't stop at the entry position.

Experience in the service industry counts, but the focus is on expression and adaptability. Prepare a story about "the most difficult customer you have ever dealt with" for the interview, which is more impressive than a list of skills.

Don’t just look at your appearance when recruiting front desk staff, you should also take a look at on-site adaptability and emotional management. Candidates who can use the system, are good at foreign languages, and can handle three shifts deserve better promotion channels.
